w10_P4_002688: A shipyard rig drives a carriage whose mass plate reads 162000 g. The drive must supply the force that gives the carriage that acceleration, and the log writes that force in kilonewtons. Three carriages run per track and 9 tracks run in the yard, so the yard demand is 3 times the logged value and then 9 times that. From the yard total 30 is subtracted, in those same kilonewton units, as the standing tare. A 55 L paint drum stands by the track and is not involved. What is the final figure, in kN?
w10_P4_002699: A steel mill audit ends with one figure in kilojoules. w10_P4_002706: A laboratory summary ends with one number in kilojoules. w10_P4_002707: A theme-park engineering report ends with a single figure in kilojoules. w10_P4_002710: A cannery packs two runs of 290 and 245 identical tins into equal full cases, using the largest case size that divides both counts exactly. w10_P4_002711: A brewery report ends with one figure in kilojoules. w10_P4_002712: A joinery audit ends with one number in kilonewtons. w10_P4_002743: An archery club's tally ends with one number in joules.
